title: Adaptive per-entity circuit guards and staged fallback playbook
creator: Aisha Kapoor
description: Implement an adaptive circuit-breaker system that computes per-entity (dependency, model, tenant) trip thresholds from observed SLO exposure and traffic shape, applies smoothing and hysteresis to avoid flapping, and orchestrates staged safe fallback behavior across regions and model variants. Goal: keep global SLOs intact while minimizing correctness regressions and customer-visible errors during resource pressure or dependency outages.
background: We currently have coarse, static trippoints for some model endpoints and tenant-level quotas. Incidents in the past 12 months show: (1) single-tenant traffic spikes can cause noisy neighbor impact, (2) regional infra degradation leads to poorly coordinated failovers that overload fallthrough paths, and (3) static thresholds either trip too late (causing SLO misses) or too early (unnecessary degradation). We need an automated, observable, and testable per-entity guard that uses SLO-derived budgets and progressive fallback choreography.
acceptance_criteria: Per-entity trip thresholds computed from: error_budget = max(0, target_error_rate - observed_error_rate) aggregated over 1h and 24h windows

Soft-trip and hard-trip modes implemented with configurable hysteresis: soft-trip reduces per-tenant concurrency by X% and routes a fraction f of traffic to model-variant fallback; hard-trip rejects or queues according to customer tier
Fallback chain supports: local cache return, downgraded model variant (quantized/cheaper), cross-region routing, and finally synthetic graceful degradation response with clear client-side signal
Automated canary rollout for the adaptive guards with observability dashboards and rollback hooks in Console
End-to-end tests that simulate tenant spikes, regional outage, and dependency slowness and verify no more than 5% incremental SLO violations vs baseline when fallback is active
decisions: Use SLO-derived error budgets as primary signal for thresholds (decision made 2026-03-04): error_budget_h = target_error_rate - observed_error_rate_1h; error_budget_24h for longer-term behavior
Implement dual-window monitoring (1h and 24h) with weighted aggregation (0.7 * 1h + 0.3 * 24h) to balance reactivity and stability
Soft-trip will initially be a probabilistic shed (token-bucket based) that reduces concurrency for noisy tenants instead of immediate hard rejects to preserve request completion where possible
Cross-region failover only used after local fallback exhaustion; prefer model-variant downgrade before cross-region to reduce cost and cold-start risk
Circuit config stored in central config service with per-entity override keys and default inheritance (global -> region -> tenant -> model)
tradeoffs: Aggressive early shedding reduces SLO violations but increases correctness regression risk from downgraded models
Cross-region routing improves availability but increases latency and inter-region egress cost; therefore it is a last-resort action
Probabilistic soft-trip reduces user-visible errors compared to hard rejects but complicates troubleshooting determinism
implementation_notes: Threshold calc: use moving quantile estimator (P95 latency, P99 error rate) with exponential decay factor alpha=0.2 for immediate responsiveness
Hysteresis windows: enter soft-trip if 1h-weighted_budget < soft_threshold for 3 consecutive 1m buckets; clear only after 10m of healthy buckets
Token-bucket for probabilistic shed: bucket_rate per-tenant set to proportional share of reserved throughput, fallback_fraction ramped from 5%->50% over 15 minutes
Fallback chain encoding: [local_cache, model_variant:q4_8, model_variant:int8_fast, cross_region:region-b, degrade_response]. Each step has TTLs and backoff timers
Ensure KV cache is consulted before downgrade to minimize correctness loss
testing_plan: Unit tests for threshold math and hysteresis logic
Integration tests simulating spike from single tenant using load-generator against dedicated pool
Chaos test: kill region-a GPU fleet and verify staged fallback routes 80% traffic to downgraded variant and 20% to cross-region within 90s
Regression test: ensure canary path does not increase baseline error_rate by >2% for tier-1 customers
Load tests with 4k rps for mixed-tenancy to calibrate token-bucket and fallback_fraction ramps
rollout_plan: Feature-flag gated rollout: start with opt-in tenants and internal canaries (10 tenants) for 48h
Stage 2: expand to 30% of traffic in non-critical regions for 7 days
Stage 3: global rollout with dynamic limits and per-tenant opt-out option
Rollback criteria: sustained >3% increase in P90 latency or >1% absolute increase in error_rate for enterprise customers over 1h
observability_and_alerts: Console dashboard: per-entity trip state heatmap, fallback chain counts, percent traffic routed to each fallback step
Alerts: (1) soft-trip activation count spike > X/min, (2) hard-trip activation > Y/min, (3) cross-region fallback rate > 2% of total ingress
SLO reports tied to incidents with automatic attach of last 24h guard configs and triggered rules
security_and_compliance_notes: Cross-region routing must respect tenant data residency tags. config service enforces blocklist for tenants that disallow egress
Fallback responses must not leak internal debug info; synthetic degrade payloads must carry only pre-approved templates
open_questions: How should multi-model ensembles be treated when one model is degraded? (route to ensemble with degraded member or recompute weights?)
Should we support dynamic per-tenant SLA tiers that change soft/hard thresholds automatically based on billing tier?
What's the appropriate default for fallback_fraction ramp speed for bursty workloads?
